intro.t: Forty years of saying what nobody wanted to hear.
b: Jeremiah warns Judah for decades, is beaten, imprisoned and thrown into a cistern for it, and watches Jerusalem fall anyway. The most personally exposed of the prophets — his complaints to God are preserved alongside his preaching.
Chapter 31 contains the promise of a new covenant written on hearts, which Jesus takes up at the Last Supper.

1.t: Jeremiah objects that he is too young. He will be right about almost everything and heeded about nothing.
An almond branch and a boiling pot. God promises to make him a fortified city, which implies what is coming.

17.h: Like a tree planted by water
17.t: The same image as Psalm 1, and it does not promise the absence of heat but the absence of anxiety in it.
A diagnosis, not a slogan. It explains why the covenant of chapter 31 has to be internal.

29.h: Seek the peace of the city
29.t: Build houses, plant gardens, and pray for Babylon's welfare. Instructions for living faithfully in a place you did not choose.
Spoken to exiles who have just been told to settle down and build houses because they will be there seventy years. The promise is real and its timescale is rarely quoted with it.

31.t: I have drawn you with unfailing kindness. The verse immediately before the new covenant promise.
Written on hearts, with sins remembered no more. Jesus takes the phrase at the Last Supper, and Hebrews quotes the passage twice.

20.t: Jeremiah accuses God of overpowering him, then says the word is like fire in his bones and he cannot hold it in. Both are in the same paragraph.

32.t: With Babylon at the gates, Jeremiah buys land as a sign that houses and fields will be bought here again. Prophecy performed rather than spoken.

2.t: They have forsaken the spring of living water and dug their own cisterns, broken ones. Idolatry described as bad engineering.

7.t: Do not trust in deceptive words: the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD. Jesus quotes verse 11 when he clears the temple.

9.t: Boast in understanding and knowing the LORD. Paul quotes it twice to the Corinthians.

15.t: And I ate them; they were my joy and my heart's delight. Said by a man whose ministry brought him nothing but trouble.

23.t: Against Israel's leaders, followed by the promise of a righteous Branch from David. Ezekiel 34 makes the same move.

33.h: Call to me and I will answer
33.t: And tell you great and unsearchable things you do not know. Spoken while Jeremiah was under arrest.

38.t: Jeremiah sinks into the mud and is rescued by Ebed-Melech, a foreign official, using rags for padding under his arms. The detail is preserved because someone remembered it.

3.t: I am merciful, declares the LORD, I will not be angry for ever. Mercy offered in the middle of an indictment.

5.t: Jeremiah is told to search Jerusalem for a single honest man. He tries the poor, then the leaders, and finds none.

6.h: Peace, peace, where there is no peace
6.t: The charge against prophets and priests who dress the wound of the people as though it were not serious.

8.h: Is there no balm in Gilead
8.t: The question behind the spiritual. Jeremiah's grief is for a wound he cannot heal.

10.t: They cannot speak and must be carried because they cannot walk. A cucumber field is the image Jeremiah chooses.

12.h: Why does the way of the wicked prosper
12.t: Jeremiah's complaint, and God's answer is not comfort: if you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out, how will you compete with horses.

18.t: The vessel is reshaped rather than discarded. Paul draws on the image in Romans 9.

25.t: The span Daniel is reading about in Daniel 9, and the basis for the return under Cyrus.

30.h: I will restore you to health
30.t: Because they called you an outcast, Zion for whom no one cares. The reason given is the contempt of others.

36.t: Jehoiakim cuts it up column by column and throws it in the fire. Jeremiah dictates it again, with more added.

39.t: The walls breached, the king blinded, the city burned. Ebed-Melech is spared because he trusted God.

45.t: Should you seek great things for yourself? Do not. A short, bracing word to the man who wrote the scroll.

52.t: Jehoiachin released from prison and given a seat at the king's table. Jeremiah ends, like Kings, on a very small hope.

4.t: Jeremiah describes the earth returning to formless and void — creation undone. The same Hebrew words as Genesis 1:2.

11.t: Jeremiah discovers a plot against him from his own home town. The image anticipates Isaiah 53.

13.t: Buried by a river until it rots. Israel was meant to cling to God like a belt and has become useless.

14.h: Do not pray for this people
14.t: God tells the prophet to stop interceding. One of the starkest verses in the book. Worth talking through with a pastor or a mature Christian you trust.

16.t: Jeremiah is told not to take a wife or have children, as a sign of the coming catastrophe. His whole life becomes the message.

19.t: Smashed before the elders. What is shattered this way cannot be repaired.

21.h: The way of life and the way of death
21.t: Surrender to Babylon and live. The prophet's counsel sounded like treason.

22.h: Woe to him who builds by injustice
22.t: A king building a palace with unpaid labour. To defend the poor, God says, is what it means to know me.

24.t: The exiles are the good figs; those left behind are the bad. The opposite of what everyone assumed.

26.t: He is saved because some elders remember that Micah prophesied the same thing a century earlier and was not killed.

27.t: Jeremiah wears an ox yoke as a sign to submit to Babylon.

28.t: A false prophet breaks Jeremiah's wooden yoke and promises release in two years. He dies within the year, as Jeremiah said.

34.t: Judah releases its slaves under covenant and then reclaims them. God calls it profaning his name.

35.t: A family who kept their ancestor's command for centuries, held up as a rebuke to Judah who would not keep God's.

37.h: Is there any word from the LORD
37.t: The king asks secretly. Jeremiah answers honestly, from prison, and then asks not to be sent back to the dungeon.

40.t: Offered a comfortable life in Babylon, he chooses to stay with the poor left in the ruined land.

41.t: The governor left in charge is murdered at dinner. The remnant falls apart.

42.t: The survivors ask Jeremiah to seek God's will, promise to obey, and when the answer is 'stay', they go to Egypt.

43.t: Jeremiah is carried off against his will by the people he warned. His ministry ends in exile in the land Israel was rescued from.

44.t: The refugees blame their disasters on stopping worship of a pagan goddess. Honest reasoning, entirely wrong.

46.t: The first of the oracles against the nations, which run to chapter 51.

47.h: Sword of the LORD, how long
47.t: A cry of pity in an oracle of judgement against the Philistines.

48.t: Like a flute. The prophet grieves even for enemies.

49.t: I will keep them alive. Mercy inside an oracle against Edom.

50.h: They will ask the way to Zion
50.t: Israel and Judah returning together, weeping, joining themselves to God in an everlasting covenant.

51.t: Tied to a stone and sunk: so Babylon will sink and not rise. The words of Jeremiah end here.
